title: Rapid Grok: SDK first-10-minutes playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a rapid, tactical playbook for a 10-minute developer loop to 'grok' the Redwood SDK and ship a single observable call from a sample app. The goal is maximal signal for lowest cognitive overhead: get a token-generation request running locally, see telemetry, and have a concise guardrail list for follow-ups.

Audience:
- New engineers (first contact)
- Solutions engineers doing quick demos
- Docs writers who need a reproducible first-run flow

Principles (GROK loop):
1) Read: one very short example that shows the call shape and envs.
2) Run: run the example end-to-end in <10 minutes.
3) Observe: confirm telemetry and one metric (latency or error rate).
Repeat if something fails; each loop should add one small fix.

Quick path (10-minute checklist):
- Prereqs: node 18+, docker (optional), API key in REDWOOD_API_KEY.
- Clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk.git --branch rapid-grok
- Install: cd sdk/examples/rapid-grok && npm ci
- File: create .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-... and REDWOOD_ENV=local
- Start: node quickstart.js
- Smoke: curl localhost:3000/ask -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
- Verify: open http://localhost:3000/telemetry (local server exposes condensed telemetry)

one-file quickstart example (quickstart.js) - description only:
- purpose: single file that demonstrates full loop: build request, call SDK, stream tokens, emit one telemetry event to local agent.
- behaviour: logs succinct lines: START -> TOKENS -> END -> TELEMETRY(EVENT_ID)
- failure modes: shows clear error messages for auth, network, and model-not-found.

Minimal sample curl (for docs snippet):
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-lite-1","input":"Summarize this in one line: Redwood is..."}'
- expected: 200 + json {"id":"...","output":"..."}

Local dev conventions to include in quickstart:
- ENV names: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV (local|staging|prod), REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL
- Telemetry: export REDWOOD_TELEM_ADDR=http://localhost:4001 for local agent capture
- Ports: sample app defaults to 3000 for app, 4001 for telemetry agent

Telemetry and observability (must-have for first 10 min):
- Emit: one event with fields: event_type, latency_ms, success(boolean), sample_rate (defaults to 1.0 locally)
- Local agent: built-in small HTTP endpoint that writes last 50 events to /telemetry
- Verify: quick assert in the sample script that last event success==true and latency_ms < 2000ms (adjust depending on network)

Docs structure recommendation (for the first-10-minutes page):
- TL;DR (1–2 lines) + single copy-paste block (one-file script)
- Pre-reqs (2 bullets)
- Step-by-step run (6 bullets) with exact commands
- Verify (how to check telemetry and output)
- Troubleshooting quick table (Auth, Network, Model mismatch)

Troubleshooting quick notes:
- Auth: "401 Unauthorized" -> check REDWOOD_API_KEY value, no trailing spaces, key active (RDW console).
- Network: DNS failures -> try REDWOOD_ENV=local to hit runner-proxy, or run with --offline-sim.
- Model mismatch: SDK will suggest nearest compatible model; quickstart recommends passing model=redwood/small-v1 for consistent behavior.

Acceptance criteria for this playbook to ship to docs: (small checklist)
- [ ] Single-file quickstart exists and runs on mac/linux without extra deps
- [ ] Telemetry endpoint included and sample asserts pass
- [ ] Copy-paste curl snippet for hosted API works with prod key
- [ ] Troubleshooting table present and actionable
- [ ] Docs page size <= 600 words (concise)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want the quickstart to include a streaming tokens demo by default? Pros: shows magic; Cons: more moving parts. Propose: streaming as "optional next step".
- Should the local agent be a separate npm package or live in examples/? (pref: examples/ for low friction; later promote to @redwood/telemetry-agent)
- Link to the onboarding dashboard for creating API keys: where is the canonical URL? (ask product/docs)

Next actions (owners):
- Maya: draft quickstart.js and docs page (due +3 days)
- Alex: add a minimal local-telemetry-agent in examples/ (due +5 days)
- Priya: write the short troubleshooting table and one-sentence summary for the top-of-page (due +3 days)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep friction below 3 commands to run. If we need a CLI, name it redwood-init and limit prompts.
- Example outputs should be stable; avoid random seed text that varies too much for screenshots.
summary: A short, tactical playbook for a 10-minute SDK first-run (grok) that prioritizes a single-file demo, observable telemetry, and a tiny troubleshooting checklist. Draft status, owners and next steps listed.
